premises: The source defines one electron-volt as an electron's energy gain through a one-volt accelerating potential difference.
The saved NIST observation supplies elementary charge magnitude e = 1.602176634e-19 C exactly, independently of author candidates.
One volt is one joule per coulomb.
electron_volt.charge_and_sign: Kinetic energy gain is electric work q*(V_initial-V_final); with an accelerating potential magnitude use |q|*|Delta V|. For protons q=+e; an electron must move in the accelerating sense for its negative charge. Do not claim positive gain for an arbitrary signed potential difference.
electron_volt.independent_verdict: The original 1.60207e-10 J is inconsistent by approximately nine orders of magnitude; neither its mantissa nor exponent is the exact modern conversion.

cyclotron_and_ring.nonrelativistic: For transverse circular motion |q|vB=m0*v^2/R, so T=2*pi*m0/(|q|B); at fixed B this is independent of R and v only in the v<<c regime.
cyclotron_and_ring.relativistic: m0 is invariant under acceleration of the same particle; gamma=1/sqrt(1-v^2/c^2), momentum p=gamma*m0*v. Historical m=gamma*m0 means relativistic mass, not a changing rest mass.
cyclotron_and_ring.bending: |q|vB=p*v/R gives p=|q|BR. Fixed bending radius requires B to increase as momentum increases.
cyclotron_and_ring.timing: For the fixed ring path length C, f_rev=v/C. At fixed RF harmonic h, f_RF=h*v/C must track arrival phase; it increases as v increases and approaches a limit as v approaches c. The gap field must do positive work on arriving protons.
cyclotron_and_ring.terminology: A fixed-radius ring with a ramped guide field and synchronized RF is a proton synchrotron-type machine. Do not turn the historical Chinese heading into a fixed-B, decreasing-RF-frequency synchrocyclotron description.

historical_quantities.dubna: One hundred yi electron-volts = 1e10 eV = 10 GeV; retain the Dubna Joint Institute facility and Figure 228б reference in historical context.
historical_quantities.serpukhov: Retain 20000 metric tonnes of magnets, approximately 1.5 km circumference, 350000 V effective accelerating potential per revolution, 350000 eV proton gain per revolution, and greater than 700 yi eV = greater than 7e10 eV over the full acceleration cycle.
historical_quantities.work_check: A singly charged proton across 350000 V gains e*350000 V = 350000 eV; per-revolution gain is not the entire acceleration-cycle energy.
historical_quantities.time_and_country: The original 'our country/current largest' is the Soviet source's historical perspective, not China or a present-day 2026 ranking. Do not add an independently unverified contemporary facility ranking.
